core_obligations: Show that a perfect M, represented by a bounded complex of finite projective modules, has a left dual in the category of complexes and hence in D(R) (proof lines 38594-38598).
Assume a left dual (N, eta, epsilon) and choose a complex M^bullet representing M together with a K-flat complex N^bullet with flat terms representing N (proof lines 38601-38606).

Write eta as a map of complexes R -> Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet) and express the image of 1 as a finite sum of tensors m_{n,i} tensor n_{-n,i} with m_{n,i} in M^n and n_{-n,i} in N^{-n} (proof lines 38607-38615).

Form the subcomplex K^bullet of M^bullet generated by the m_{n,i} and their differentials, observe that Tot(K^bullet tensor_R N^bullet) sits inside Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet) and contains eta(1), and hence that eta factors through K tensor^L N (proof lines 38616-38624).

Use the identity (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) = id_M and the displayed commutative diagram to conclude that the identity on M factors through K, so that M lies in D^-(R) (proof lines 38625-38641).

Re-represent M by a bounded above complex of free modules, repeat the finite-sum construction to find a bounded subcomplex K^bullet of finite free modules containing all the m_{n,i}, and again factor the identity on M through K (proof lines 38642-38651).
Conclude that M is perfect because it is a summand of the perfect complex K (proof lines 38652-38653).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the perfect objects of D(R) as exactly those admitting a left dual, and identifies that dual with the object M^vee of the dual-perfect-complex lemma (source lines 38580-38591). One direction is structural: a bounded complex of finite projective modules has a left dual already in the category of complexes (proof lines 38594-38598). The converse is the hard direction and occupies the rest of the proof. From a left dual (N, eta, epsilon) one chooses a representative M^bullet and a K-flat complex N^bullet with flat terms, writes eta(1) as a finite sum of tensors m_{n,i} tensor n_{-n,i}, and builds the subcomplex K^bullet generated by the m_{n,i} and their differentials (proof lines 38601-38622). The key move is that eta factors through K tensor^L N and the identity on M therefore factors through K, which forces M to lie in D^-(R) (proof lines 38623-38641). One then re-represents M by a bounded above complex of free modules, uses the same finite-sum expression to cut out a bounded subcomplex K^bullet consisting of finite free modules, and again factors the identity through K; since K is perfect and a summand of M, M is perfect (proof lines 38642-38653). The non-routine content is the factoring-of-the-identity trick applied twice, once to bound M above and once to bound it below.
